memory_breakdown.distinction_note: In native LXC OS-level virtualization, the configured memory limit is a Linux cgroups v2 boundary (memory.max) enforced by the kernel's memory management subsystem. Unlike KVM (virtio-balloon) or VirtualBox (hypervisor guest allocation), LXC allocates zero memory upfront. Memory consumption represents actual resident pages (memory.current and RSS) dynamically allocated by processes executing directly on the host kernel.
